answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful stake in escrow, like a quartz deposit that is hard to fake at scale: creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand deposits, so the attack cost grows linearly while its benefit stays flat. Identities that misbehave lose the stake, and reputation accrues slowly, so a fresh identity starts at its nadir with no trust. Over time, honest agents build a solid record, as durable as marble, while cheap clones stay worthless because they cannot buy history without paying the same price again.
